# bbsrgeo

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

`bbsrgeo` downloads the **area crosswalks** ("Umstiegsschluessel") for
municipalities and districts published by the BBSR (Bundesinstitut fuer
Bau-, Stadt- und Raumforschung, Germany's Federal Institute for Research on
Building, Urban Affairs and Spatial Development), and uses them to convert
German regional statistics time series (e.g. from the Regionaldatenbank
Deutschland / GENESIS-Regio) onto a consistent, freely chosen set of area
boundaries - despite municipality mergers and district reorganizations.

More background and a worked example: `vignette("bbsrgeo")`.

## Installation

`bbsrgeo` is not (yet) on CRAN. Install from the local source directory:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("local::.")
```

## Example

```{r example}
library(bbsrgeo)
library(dplyr)

# Which crosswalks does the BBSR offer for districts?
bbsr_crosswalk_available("districts")
```

`bbsrgeo` ships with a real example dataset, `example_population` - GENESIS-Regio
population figures for every German district, 1995-2024, each on the area
boundary that was actually valid at the time. Sachsen-Anhalt's Saalkreis and
Landkreis Merseburg-Querfurt, for example, merged into the new Saalekreis on
2007-07-01:

```{r}
example_population |>
  filter(district_name %in% c("Saalkreis", "Merseburg-Querfurt, Kreis", "Saalekreis")) |>
  filter(year %in% 2005:2008) |>
  select(ags, district_name, year, population_total) |>
  arrange(year, ags)
```

`harmonize_regions()` converts this onto a single, consistent boundary using
the real BBSR crosswalk:

```{r}
path <- bbsr_crosswalk_download(level = "districts", kind = "annual")
crosswalk <- bbsr_crosswalk_read(path)

harmonize_regions(
  example_population,
  crosswalk = crosswalk,
  ags_col = "ags",
  year_col = "year",
  value_cols = "population_total",
  type = "absolute",
  weight = "population",
  target_year = "current",
  level = "districts"
) |>
  filter(ags == "15088000", year %in% 2005:2008)
```

Saalkreis and Merseburg-Querfurt's populations are now combined into
Saalekreis for every year, comparable across the boundary reform.
